title: DDoS Attack with Suspected Data Exfiltration
description: Abnormal traffic is flooding auth endpoints while simultaneously a background process is making unusual outbound connections. You must: rate-limit the attack, investigate potential data exfiltration, escalate to the security team, and preserve forensic evidence – all while keeping the service available.

initial_alerts.message: auth-service: 48,000 req/s on /api/auth/login (normal: 200 req/s). Possible credential stuffing or DDoS.
api-gateway: WAF detected 312 distinct source IPs hammering /api/auth/login with rotating user-agents
auth-service: CPU at 94%, p99 latency 8,200ms. Legitimate users experiencing login failures.
user-db: Unusual SELECT volume – 3x baseline reads on users table in last 5 minutes
data-pipeline: Outbound network egress spike – 2.4 GB transferred to 185.220.101.0/24 (Tor exit node range) in last 3 minutes

auth-service.message: Rate limit exceeded for IP 185.220.101.14: 2847 requests in 60s on /api/auth/login
Rate limit exceeded for IP 185.220.101.47: 2312 requests in 60s on /api/auth/login
Credential stuffing pattern detected: 847 unique usernames attempted from 185.220.101.0/24 subnet
auth-service: login success rate 0.8% (normal: 94%). Possible credential stuffing in progress.
DB connection pool saturating: 98/100 connections in use

api-gateway.message: WAF ALERT: Botnet signature match on 312 IPs. User-agent rotation: curl/7.x, python-requests/2.x, Mozilla/5.0 (rotating). Destination: /api/auth/login
DDoS mitigation NOT active – no rate limit rule configured for /api/auth/login at IP-block level
Legitimate traffic origin mix: 94% normal users, 6% flagged IPs in last 10 min

user-db.message: Slow query: SELECT email, password_hash, pii_data FROM users LIMIT 100000 — executed by user: data_pipeline_svc (not auth-service)
Bulk SELECT on users table: 847,293 rows returned in last 3 minutes from connection user=data_pipeline_svc
Normal auth queries from auth-service: individual lookups by email (expected pattern)

data-pipeline.message: Unusual job triggered: export_users_full_v2 – not in scheduled job list. Job parameters: destination=s3://external-bucket-xf92k, include_pii=true
Outbound connection to 185.220.101.0/24 (Tor exit node). Transferring 2.4GB. This IP range is flagged in threat intel.
Job export_users_full_v2 started by API key: dpk_f8a2c... (key created 2024-03-20T03:18:00Z – 4 minutes ago)

auth-service-audit.message: Successful login: user=admin@company.com from IP 185.220.101.89 – ANOMALOUS (not a known admin IP)
API key dpk_f8a2c... created by admin@company.com – this key has data-pipeline write access

diagnostic_results.netstat data-pipeline: Active outbound connections: 185.220.101.14:443 (ESTABLISHED, 847MB sent), 185.220.101.47:443 (ESTABLISHED, 1.2GB sent), 185.220.101.89:443 (ESTABLISHED, 0.4GB sent). All Tor exit nodes.
diagnostic_results.threat_intel 185.220.101.0/24: Threat intel: 185.220.101.0/24 is a known Tor exit node range. Associated with data exfiltration campaigns in 3 CVE reports (2023-2024). HIGH confidence malicious.
diagnostic_results.check_api_keys data-pipeline: API key dpk_f8a2c... created 03:18 UTC by compromised admin account. Permissions: read:users (PII), write:pipeline-jobs, execute:exports. RECOMMENDATION: revoke immediately.
diagnostic_results.check_job_history data-pipeline: Scheduled jobs: daily_analytics (04:00 UTC), weekly_report (Sunday 06:00 UTC). Job export_users_full_v2 is NOT a scheduled job – triggered via API.
diagnostic_results.waf_rules api-gateway: Current WAF rules: SQL injection block, XSS block. No IP-based rate limiting on /api/auth/login. No subnet blocking rules active.
diagnostic_results.network_capture auth-service: Packet sample: 48,247 req/s to /api/auth/login. Source IPs: 185.220.101.0/24 subnet (312 unique IPs). All requests include X-Forwarded-For headers suggesting botnet.

rate_limit_auth_endpoint.description: Apply IP-based rate limit: max 10 req/min per IP on /api/auth/login
rate_limit_auth_endpoint.note: Rate limit rule applied. Traffic on /api/auth/login: 48,000 req/s → 2,100 req/s. auth-service CPU: 94% → 31%. Legitimate users can now log in. Attack traffic reduced but not eliminated.

block_tor_subnet.description: Block entire 185.220.101.0/24 subnet at WAF level
block_tor_subnet.note: Subnet 185.220.101.0/24 blocked at WAF. Attack traffic dropped 89%. Some legitimate Tor users also blocked – acceptable tradeoff during incident.

revoke_api_key.description: Revoke compromised API key dpk_f8a2c... immediately
revoke_api_key.note: API key dpk_f8a2c... revoked. data-pipeline job export_users_full_v2 terminated. Outbound transfer stopped at 2.4GB. Forensic snapshot of transferred data logged.

isolate_data_pipeline.description: Network-isolate data-pipeline service to stop active exfiltration
isolate_data_pipeline.note: data-pipeline network access revoked. All outbound connections terminated. Active exfiltration stopped. Service offline until investigation complete.

preserve_forensics.description: Capture network logs, job history, and API key audit trail before remediation
preserve_forensics.note: Forensic snapshot captured: network pcap (2.4GB sample), job logs, API key creation audit trail, user-db query logs. Evidence preserved for security team.

escalate_security_team.description: Page security team with full incident summary
escalate_security_team.note: Security team paged. Incident severity: P0. Security on-call responding. Handoff: compromised admin account, 2.4GB PII exfil to Tor nodes, DDoS as distraction.

reset_admin_password.description: Force password reset for admin@company.com and invalidate all sessions
reset_admin_password.note: admin@company.com sessions invalidated, password reset forced. Attacker access via compromised account revoked.

grader_criteria.understanding_required: Agent must recognize DDoS is a distraction for exfiltration – both must be addressed
